events.title: King John Seals Magna Carta
events.description: On the meadow at Runnymede near the Thames, England's King John affixed his seal to the Magna Carta. Rebellious barons had forced him to agree to its terms.
events.significance: The charter established the principle that even a king must obey the law. It became a cornerstone of constitutional government and influenced later documents, including the U.S. Constitution.

events.title: Arkansas Becomes the 25th State
events.description: Arkansas was admitted to the Union as the 25th state. It was the third state carved from the vast Louisiana Purchase territory.
events.significance: Its admission extended the nation's reach across the Mississippi Valley. It also formed part of the broader pattern of westward expansion and the sectional balance between slave and free states.

events.title: Arlington National Cemetery Is Established
events.description: During the Civil War, Secretary of War Edwin Stanton designated Arlington as a national military cemetery. It began on 200 acres of land overlooking Washington, D.C.
events.significance: The site has grown to more than 600 acres. It is now the nation's best-known resting place for fallen service members and a place of remembrance.

events.title: U.S. Marines Land on Saipan
events.description: Some 40,000 Marines from the Second and Fourth Marine Divisions stormed ashore on Saipan in the Mariana Islands. The battle lasted until July 9.
events.significance: Capturing Saipan gave the United States air bases within bomber range of the Japanese home islands. It was a major turning point in the Pacific War.
